input.question: Light Reflection : To maximize bedroom light, do I turn the bathroom light on or close the bathroom door? [w/ Diagram]
input.ground_truth: Well, this is a problem that can only really be solved by experiment! Especially since we have no idea about a lot of the factors involved (the exact geometry of the rooms, the exact optical properties of the paint/wallpaper, etc etc). The simplest way to measure I can think of would be to use my DSLR with a set exposure time and just take pictures of my desk with the door open and then closed, since that's a fairly objective way to measure how bright it is. If you don't have a DSLR, have fun, come up with your own experiment. Isolate what you're trying to measure as best you can and have at it!

Question: Light Reflection : To maximize bedroom light, do I turn the bathroom light on or close the bathroom door? [w/ Diagram]

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine your bedroom and bathroom are next to each other, like two rooms that are neighbors.

If you want your **bedroom to be brighter (have more light)**, you want as much light as possible to come into your bedroom.

Now, let’s think about the bathroom light:

- If you **turn on the bathroom light** but **keep the bathroom door OPEN**, the light from the bathroom can come into your bedroom. That means more light for your bedroom! 🌞

- But if you **close the bathroom door**, the light from the bathroom can’t get into your bedroom anymore. So your bedroom might be a little darker. 🚪🔇

So, **to make your bedroom the brightest**, you should **turn on the bathroom light AND leave the bathroom door open** (if it’s safe to do so). That way, the light can travel from the bathroom into your bedroom and make it brighter!

But if you want the bathroom to be private or don’t want the bathroom light shining into your bedroom, then you can close the door. But if your only goal is to have the most light in your bedroom, **leave the door open and turn on the bathroom light!**
